meta.title: RFC 8555 ACME hypergraph
meta.frame: Built from RFC 8555 (with RFC 8737 for tls-alpn-01), scoped to the core certificate-issuance flow. Nodes are atomic protocol facts in PKI / certificate-management domain language; edges are typed, possibly n-ary relationships over a closed vocabulary. The order, authorization, and challenge state machines are modelled as transitions_to edges with the trigger in the rationale.
meta.note: Spec-reference graph: RFC 8555 (with RFC 8737 for tls-alpn-01) scoped to the core certificate-issuance flow, in PKI / certificate-management domain language. This is a map of the PROTOCOL as specified, not of this repo's code -- unlike ontology/acme-cert-lifecycle-domain.json (the codebase ubiquitous-language ontology, evidence-cited to symbols). Companion prose: doc/RFC8555_ACME_PROTOCOL_GRAPH.md and doc/RFC_COMPLIANCE.md. Nodes are atomic protocol facts; edges are the binary projection of typed, possibly n-ary hyperedges (grouped by hyperedge_id; the n-ary grouping lives in the .md). The order / authorization / challenge state machines are modelled as transitions_to edges with the trigger in the rationale.

relation_types.is_a: source is a kind of target
relation_types.precedes: source reliably occurs before target in the protocol sequence
relation_types.causes: a change in source produces a change in target; see sign
relation_types.enables: source is a precondition that makes target possible
relation_types.constrains: source sets a guard, ceiling, or rejection condition on target; see sign
relation_types.determines: source is a formal input to target's definition or value
relation_types.authenticates: source cryptographically establishes the origin / legitimacy of target (added for RFC 8555)
relation_types.proves_control_of: source demonstrates the requester's practical control over the identifier target (added for RFC 8555)
relation_types.authorizes: source is the standing permission that the target operation consumes; kept distinct from enables because authorization is a first-class ACME object (added for RFC 8555)
relation_types.transitions_to: state-machine edge: source status becomes target status on the trigger named in the rationale (added for RFC 8555)

nodes.label: The ACME client acts for the certificate applicant and holds the account key pair; it originates every protocol request
The ACME server is the CA; it issues nonces, registers accounts, creates authorizations, runs validation, and issues certificates
The directory is the ACME entry point; a GET returns the URLs for newNonce, newAccount, newOrder, newAuthz, revokeCert, keyChange, plus a meta object
An account object represents the client's registration and binds the account public key to a status, a contact list, and the termsOfServiceAgreed flag
An order object represents one certificate request, carrying identifiers, authorization URLs, a finalize URL, an expires timestamp, a status, and (once issued) a certificate URL
An authorization object is the CA's per-identifier grant to an account; it holds the identifier, a challenges list, a status, and (when valid) a required expires timestamp
A challenge object is one offered proof-of-control method inside an authorization, carrying type, token, url, and status
The certificate resource is the issued PEM certificate chain, fetched by POST-as-GET from the order's certificate URL
A replay nonce is a single-use server value delivered in the Replay-Nonce header and obtained from newNonce; responses carrying it are marked no-store
The account key pair is generated client-side; its public key is registered on the account and its private key signs every subsequent request
Every ACME POST body is a JWS whose protected header carries alg, nonce, url, and exactly one of jwk or kid
nodes.qualifier: Flattened JSON Serialization; no detached payload; no unprotected header

nodes.label: newAccount and revokeCert carry the full public key in the jwk header; every other request carries kid = the account URL
Order finalization submits a base64url PKCS#10 CSR whose requested names must match the order's identifiers
The key authorization is token + "." + base64url(SHA-256(account-key JWK thumbprint)), binding a challenge token to the account key
An identifier is a {type:"dns", value:<domain>} pair naming a name to be certified; wildcard authorizations set wildcard:true
http-01: the client serves the key authorization as the body of http://<domain>/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>
dns-01: the client publishes a TXT record at _acme-challenge.<domain> whose value is base64url(SHA-256(key authorization)); the only method valid for wildcards
nodes.qualifier: only method valid for wildcard identifiers

nodes.label: tls-alpn-01: the client serves a self-signed certificate carrying the key-authorization digest via the acme-tls/1 ALPN protocol on port 443
newNonce: a HEAD or GET that returns a fresh Replay-Nonce and nothing else
newAccount: a jwk-signed POST with contact and termsOfServiceAgreed; a 201 returns the account URL in the Location header
newOrder: a POST of the identifiers list; a 201 returns a pending order with its authorization URLs and finalize URL
The client POST-as-GETs each authorization URL to read its challenge list and pick one method
The client POSTs an empty object to the chosen challenge URL to signal the proof is provisioned and validation may start
On challenge response the CA connects to the identifier (HTTP path, DNS TXT, or TLS-ALPN) and compares the retrieved artifact to the expected key authorization, with retries
Once the order is ready the client POSTs the CSR to the order's finalize URL
The client POST-as-GETs the order's certificate URL to download the PEM chain
Each nonce is single-use; a stale or unknown nonce is rejected with badNonce and a fresh nonce is supplied for retry
The JWS protected "url" header must equal the HTTP request URL, binding the signature to one endpoint
When the directory meta requires it, newAccount without termsOfServiceAgreed:true does not create an account
The order's expires timestamp bounds its lifetime; past it the order is invalid
Reads of account-bound resources use POST-as-GET - a signed JWS with an empty ("") payload - not an anonymous GET
Order status "pending": at least one of the order's authorizations is not yet valid
Order status "ready": every authorization is valid and the client may finalize
Order status "processing": the CA is issuing from the submitted CSR
Order status "valid": the certificate is issued and the order's certificate URL is populated
Order status "invalid": an authorization failure/expiry, a processing error, or order expiry has terminated the order
Authorization status "pending": no challenge has yet succeeded
Authorization status "valid": one challenge succeeded; an expires timestamp is now required
Authorization status "invalid": a challenge failed or an error occurred
A valid authorization can later move to "deactivated" (client request), "expired" (expires passes), or "revoked" (server)
nodes.qualifier: post-issuance; outside the core issuance flow

nodes.label: Challenge status "pending": the client has not yet responded
Challenge status "processing": the CA is attempting validation and may retry
Challenge status "valid": the CA confirmed the proof and set the validated timestamp
Challenge status "invalid": validation failed after the CA's retries
